components.title: HP-MPC four-party malicious checks
components.summary: The protocol-specific verification layer for the paper's four-party, one-corruption malicious configuration.

components.title: SPDZ global-MAC checks and sacrifice
components.summary: Checks opened authenticated shares against a hidden global MAC key and sacrifices preprocessing candidates to detect malformed correlations.

components.title: SPDZ-secured distributed garbling
components.summary: Constructs and checks the BMR garbling inside an actively secure arithmetic MPC before the fast online evaluation.

components.title: TinyOT authenticated-bit checks
components.summary: Uses global-key bit MACs and batch checks to detect malicious deviations in Boolean two-party computation.

components.title: Verifiable sharing and degree-consistency checks
components.summary: Enforces polynomial consistency and reconstructability against Byzantine deviations under the BGW honest-majority threshold.

components.title: ABY A/B/Y conversion gates
components.summary: Converts values among arithmetic sharing, Boolean sharing, and Yao labels within one passive 2PC execution.

components.title: ABY3 arithmetic/binary/Yao conversion
components.summary: Switches replicated ring shares among arithmetic, binary, and garbled subprotocols in the three-party setting.

components.title: Arithmetic-to-BMR preprocessing bridge
components.summary: Maps arithmetic MPC outputs used during preprocessing into the seeds and tables required by the BMR garbling.

components.title: MOTION mixed-protocol conversions
components.summary: Implements modular conversions among supported passive sharing protocols for two or more parties.

components.title: FOLEAGE F4-OLE Boolean-triple generator
components.summary: Specializes PCG techniques over F4 to generate F2 multiplication triples with near-linear circuit-dependent communication in party count.

components.title: IKNP OT extension
components.summary: Amortizes many OTs from a small base-OT seed using symmetric primitives.

components.title: MASCOT OT-based arithmetic preprocessing
components.summary: Generates authenticated arithmetic multiplication triples from OT with consistency checks, replacing the original SPDZ SHE preprocessing.

components.title: Oblivious transfer for input and AND correlations
components.summary: Provides receiver-selective transfer used for garbled inputs or shared AND evaluation.

components.title: Pairwise-seed correlated randomness
components.summary: Uses seeds shared between party pairs to derive masks locally and reduce communication in replicated-sharing protocols.

components.title: Pseudorandom correlation generator
components.summary: Expands short correlated seeds locally into long protocol-specific correlations with no interaction during expansion.

components.title: SHE-generated SPDZ preprocessing
components.summary: Uses somewhat homomorphic encryption plus proofs/checks to create authenticated arithmetic preprocessing before inputs are known.

components.title: ABY3 three-party garbled evaluation
components.summary: Evaluates ABY3's Yao-domain subcomputations using the paper's two-garbler, one-evaluator three-party garbling path; it is distinct from two-party Yao evaluation and BMR distributed garbling.

components.title: BGW polynomial gate evaluation
components.summary: Uses local polynomial-share arithmetic plus interactive degree reduction and verifiable sharing under honest-majority thresholds.

components.title: BMR distributed garbling and local evaluation
components.summary: Parties jointly create a multiparty garbled circuit; once labels are delivered, each party evaluates locally in a constant-round online phase.

components.title: Beaver-triple online multiplication
components.summary: Opens masked differences against a preprocessed multiplication triple, leaving only local arithmetic and a small online exchange per multiplication layer.

components.title: GMW Boolean gate evaluation
components.summary: Evaluates XOR gates locally and interactive AND gates from oblivious-transfer-style correlations, with rounds tied to multiplicative depth.

components.title: Replicated-sharing ring multiplication
components.summary: Combines overlapping share products with pairwise randomness to multiply ring-shared values with low bandwidth in 3PC/4PC settings.

components.title: Trio and Quad masked multiplication
components.summary: Multiplies Trio and Quad masked values by distributing input-dependent and input-independent correction work so the paper's three- and four-party configurations retain their stated communication while reducing local instructions.

components.title: Yao garble-and-evaluate
components.summary: One party garbles a Boolean circuit and the other evaluates it on obliviously transferred input labels.

components.title: Asynchronous agreement and reconstruction
components.summary: Coordinates progress and reconstruction without timing bounds while tolerating the asynchronous honest-majority corruption threshold.

components.title: Honest-majority robust reconstruction
components.summary: Uses honest-majority error correction and verifiable sharing so qualified honest parties can reconstruct despite Byzantine shares.

components.title: Reconstruction with abort on failure
components.summary: Honest parties either accept a reconstructed output or detect failure and abort; fairness and guaranteed delivery are not implied.

components.title: Arithmetic circuit over a 2-power ring
components.summary: Uses native fixed-width integer arithmetic over a ring such as Z/2^kZ; field-only checks and proofs do not transfer automatically.

components.title: Arithmetic circuit over a field
components.summary: Expresses computation with field additions and multiplications, supporting polynomial sharing and triple-based multiplication.

components.title: Boolean circuit representation
components.summary: Represents a functionality as XOR/AND or general Boolean gates; depth and non-XOR count drive different protocols differently.

components.title: Mixed arithmetic/Boolean/garbled representation
components.summary: Partitions one computation across domains and makes conversion gates explicit rather than forcing every operation into one circuit type.

components.title: ABY3 three-party Yao sharing
components.summary: Stores a Boolean value in the paper's three-party Yao domain, with one evaluator holding the active wire key and two garblers holding the label material needed to construct matching garbled circuits.

components.title: Multiparty BMR superseed labels
components.summary: Distributes each wire label across parties so no single party controls the multiparty garbling.

components.title: Replicated three-party sharing
components.summary: Replicates additive share pieces across adjacent parties so one corruption leaves enough overlap for low-communication honest-majority evaluation.

components.title: SPDZ authenticated additive sharing
components.summary: Associates additive shares with shares of a global-MAC relation so openings can be checked against active deviation.

components.title: Shamir polynomial sharing
components.summary: Represents a field value as evaluations of a low-degree polynomial, enabling local linear gates and threshold reconstruction.

components.title: TinyOT authenticated bits
components.summary: Authenticates XOR shares with global-key MAC relations tailored to Boolean computation.

components.title: Trio and Quad masked sharing
components.summary: Encodes Trio and Quad values as input-dependent masked values plus differently distributed mask shares. The exact holdings differ between the three- and four-party configurations and are not ABY3 replicated sharing.

components.title: Two-party garbled wire labels
components.summary: Encodes each Boolean wire value as one of two cryptographic labels held asymmetrically by garbler and evaluator.

components.title: Unauthenticated additive sharing
components.summary: Represents a value as additive shares without the global-MAC relation of SPDZ authenticated sharing. The surrounding passive protocol and correlation source supply privacy and multiplication.

components.title: XOR/additive Boolean sharing
components.summary: Represents a bit as the XOR of party shares, making XOR gates local and pushing interaction to AND gates.

claims.paper_title: Protocols for Secure Computations
claims.title: Two-party private computation becomes a general protocol problem
claims.statement: Yao formulates and gives protocols for two parties to compute functions of private inputs while limiting what each party learns, establishing secure two-party computation as a general cryptographic task.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and protocol constructions
claims.limitations: the record does not attribute every modern garbled-circuit formalization to this paper; the exact security formulation predates contemporary simulation frameworks

claims.paper_title: How to Play ANY Mental Game
claims.title: Circuit compilation gives general MPC with explicit adversary upgrades
claims.statement: Goldreich, Micali, and Wigderson give a general circuit-based method for secure multiparty computation and separate passive evaluation from compilation techniques that enforce security against stronger adversarial behavior.
claims.source_locator: ACM book reprint (2019, Chapter 13) of STOC 1987 pp. 218–229, chapter page numbers; §2.3 (p. 311), §4 Theorem (p. 314), §4.1–§4.3 (pp. 314–322), §5 (pp. 322–323), §6.4 (p. 327)
claims.limitations: The extended abstract sketches the passive construction with the adversarial set fixed at the start (§4, p. 314) and defers the malicious-case proof to the final paper (§5, p. 322).; Round and communication costs depend on the circuit and subprotocols; later frameworks refine the security and composition contract.

claims.paper_title: Completeness Theorems for Non-Cryptographic Fault-Tolerant Distributed Computation
claims.title: Honest-majority thresholds characterize information-theoretic general MPC
claims.statement: BGW establishes unconditional general MPC over private channels for passive corruption below one half and Byzantine corruption below one third, together with matching threshold limitations in its model.
claims.source_locator: STOC 1988 pp. 1–10; Abstract (p. 1), model in Definitions and Results (p. 2), Theorems 1–4 (pp. 2–3), proof of Theorem 1 and remarks (pp. 3–5), Theorem 2 proof (p. 5), secret sharing with cheaters and verification (pp. 5–7), proof of Theorem 3 (p. 8), Theorem 4 (p. 9)
claims.limitations: thresholds are model-dependent; dishonest-majority feasibility requires different assumptions or guarantees

claims.paper_title: The Round Complexity of Secure Protocols
claims.title: Distributed garbling removes circuit depth from MPC round complexity
claims.statement: Beaver, Micali, and Rogaway construct constant-round multiparty computation by distributing garbled-circuit preparation so that the online interaction does not grow with circuit depth.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and constant-round protocol construction
claims.limitations: constant rounds do not imply constant communication; concrete costs depend on distributed garbling and cryptographic subprotocols

claims.paper_title: Efficient Multiparty Protocols Using Circuit Randomization
claims.title: Input-independent multiplication triples separate MPC preprocessing from online work
claims.statement: Beaver's circuit-randomization method uses input-independent correlated multiplication values so arithmetic products can be opened and completed online with lightweight interaction once the correlations are available.
claims.source_locator: Circuit-randomization construction for multiplication
claims.limitations: the mechanism assumes correctly generated correlations; security and cost depend on the surrounding protocol and triple generator

claims.paper_title: Asynchronous Secure Computation
claims.title: General MPC remains feasible with arbitrarily delayed messages
claims.statement: Ben-Or, Canetti, and Goldreich establish general secure computation in a completely asynchronous private-channel network with optimal resilience below one third for fail-stop faults and below one fourth for Byzantine faults.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and main asynchronous secure-computation construction
claims.limitations: the two fault types have different optimal resilience bounds; later probabilistic-error protocols reach different Byzantine thresholds; the result is not a claim for arbitrary dishonest majorities

claims.paper_title: Proactive Secret Sharing or: How to Cope With Perpetual Leakage
claims.title: Periodic share refresh prevents mobile corruptions from accumulating secrets
claims.statement: Proactive secret sharing periodically rerandomizes distributed shares without changing the protected secret, preventing an adversary that compromises different parties in different epochs from accumulating a reconstructing set.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and share-renewal protocol
claims.limitations: requires the per-epoch corruption threshold and refresh assumptions; does not itself provide a complete MPC protocol

claims.paper_title: Adaptively Secure Multi-party Computation
claims.title: Non-committing techniques secure MPC against execution-dependent corruptions
claims.statement: Canetti, Feige, Goldreich, and Naor use non-committing encryption to obtain computational MPC over insecure channels against adaptive corruptions of non-erasing parties under the paper's threshold and trapdoor assumptions.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and main adaptive-security construction
claims.limitations: the principal theorem handles fewer than one-third corruptions and notes a modification below one half; the compiler inherits its secure-channel protocol and trapdoor assumptions; proactive mobile corruption is a distinct contract

claims.paper_title: General Secure Multi-party Computation from any Linear Secret-Sharing Scheme
claims.title: Multiplicative linear secret sharing extends general MPC beyond thresholds
claims.statement: Cramer, Damgård, and Maurer construct general MPC from multiplicative linear secret-sharing schemes, extending polynomial-threshold sharing to access structures whose multiplication and robustness conditions are stated algebraically.
claims.source_locator: Abstract, introduction, and main protocol theorem
claims.limitations: security and robustness depend on the access structure and sharing properties; not every LSSS automatically satisfies the required multiplication condition

claims.paper_title: Universally Composable Security: A New Paradigm for Cryptographic Protocols
claims.title: Environment-based simulation makes concurrent protocol composition explicit
claims.statement: Canetti defines universally composable security through an external environment and proves a composition theorem that preserves protocol security when secure subroutines are replaced inside arbitrary surrounding executions.
claims.source_locator: Framework definition and universal composition theorem
claims.limitations: composition guarantees inherit the framework and setup assumptions; stand-alone security does not imply UC security

claims.paper_title: Extending Oblivious Transfers Efficiently
claims.title: Symmetric-key OT extension expands a small public-key seed into many transfers
claims.statement: IKNP extends a small number of base oblivious transfers into a large batch using primarily symmetric-key operations, reducing the public-key cost of OT-intensive secure computation.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and OT-extension protocol
claims.limitations: security inherits the base OTs and extension model; malicious security requires additional consistency mechanisms

claims.paper_title: Improved Garbled Circuit: Free XOR Gates and Applications
claims.title: A global wire-label offset makes XOR gates free in garbled circuits
claims.statement: Free-XOR correlates the two labels on every wire through one global offset so XOR gates require neither garbled ciphertexts nor cryptographic operations, concentrating garbling cost on non-XOR gates.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and Free-XOR construction
claims.limitations: security requires the stated hash/correlation assumptions; nonlinear gates still incur garbling cost

claims.paper_title: Secure Two-Party Computation Is Practical
claims.title: End-to-end co-design makes semi-honest garbled-circuit 2PC practical
claims.statement: Pinkas, Schneider, Smart, and Williams integrate circuit design, garbling, oblivious transfer, and systems optimizations into an end-to-end semi-honest two-party computation implementation evaluated on representative functions.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; system design and evaluation sections
claims.limitations: the security model is semi-honest; performance observations are bound to the paper's implementation and workloads

claims.paper_title: Complete Fairness in Multi-Party Computation Without an Honest Majority
claims.title: Boolean OR and three-party majority admit complete fairness without an honest majority
claims.statement: Gordon and Katz construct completely fair protocols tolerating any t<n corruptions for n-party Boolean OR and three-party majority under suitable cryptographic assumptions, while proving that the latter requires super-logarithmic rounds.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and main complete-fairness theorems
claims.limitations: does not overturn general fairness impossibility; results use suitable cryptographic assumptions; the three-party-majority protocol requires super-logarithmic rounds

claims.paper_title: TASTY: Tool for Automating Secure Two-partY computations
claims.title: Typed HE and garbled values support mixed-protocol description and generation
claims.statement: TASTY provides a typed protocol-description language and runtime that generate and execute semi-honest two-party computations combining additively homomorphic encryption and garbled circuits, with explicit conversions between their value representations within one computation.
claims.source_locator: IACR ePrint 2010/365 full version: §2 (model), PDF pp. 3–5; §2.3 and Figure 2, p. 5; §4–§4.1 and Figures 5–7, pp. 6–8; §6 (automatic-selection boundary), p. 12
claims.limitations: The underlying modular conversion framework and cryptographic primitives are prior building blocks, not separately claimed inventions of this atom.; Automatic compilation from a function-description language and automatic HE/GC selection are future work in §6.; No malicious or UC security guarantee, universal performance optimum, or portable benchmark ranking is admitted.

claims.paper_title: Multiparty Computation from Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption
claims.title: Authenticated arithmetic shares enable a light dishonest-majority online phase
claims.statement: SPDZ combines somewhat-homomorphic-encryption preprocessing with information-theoretic MACs on arithmetic shares, obtaining a light online phase that is statistically UC-secure against active, adaptive corruption of up to n-1 parties in its synchronous secure-channel model.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; preprocessing overview and online protocol
claims.limitations: original preprocessing uses somewhat homomorphic encryption; successful termination is not guaranteed with a dishonest majority; the optimality statements are scoped to the paper's field-size and accounting conditions

claims.paper_title: A New Approach to Practical Active-Secure Two-Party Computation
claims.title: OT-generated authenticated bits give specialized malicious Boolean 2PC
claims.statement: TinyOT builds actively secure Boolean two-party computation from OT-generated authenticated bits and shares, making XOR local and using amortized consistency checks instead of a generic malicious compiler or garbled-circuit cut-and-choose.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and authenticated-bit protocol sections
claims.limitations: relies on preprocessing and OT assumptions; the architecture is specialized to Boolean sharing

claims.paper_title: Automatic Protocol Selection in Secure Two-Party Computations
claims.title: Conversion-aware cost models drive automatic HE and garbled-circuit assignment
claims.statement: For a specified single-static-assignment intermediate program and forecast cost model, Kerschbaum, Schneider, and Schröpfer formulate assignment of operations to HE-assisted arithmetic sharing or garbled circuits with conversion costs, and give a 0–1 integer-programming formulation and a cost-decreasing greedy heuristic for choosing the mixed protocol.
claims.source_locator: IACR ePrint 2014/200 full version: §3.2–§3.4, PDF pp. 3–4; §4–§4.2, pp. 4–5; §5 and Definition 1, pp. 5–6; §5.1–§5.2 and Algorithm 1, pp. 6–7; §6 and Tables 1–2 for forecast-only evaluation context
claims.limitations: Integer-programming optimality is relative to the modeled objective; the source discusses approximation of execution costs, including neighboring-operation effects.; The greedy method starts with garbled-circuit assignments and accepts cost-decreasing changes to HE; no general approximation ratio is admitted.; Section 5 conjectures NP-hardness of the specific partitioning problem and explicitly does not prove it.; The use-case comparisons are forecast results in specified settings, not universal measured speedups or cross-system rankings.; This atom is not a general automatic compiler for all MPC representations, a new malicious or UC security theorem, or a separate garbling construction.

claims.paper_title: ABY — A Framework for Efficient Mixed-Protocol Secure Two-Party Computation
claims.title: Typed conversions compose arithmetic, Boolean, and garbled 2PC domains
claims.statement: ABY provides a two-party framework whose computation can move through explicit conversion gates among arithmetic sharing, Boolean sharing, and Yao garbling, allowing each subcomputation to use a domain-specific cost profile.
claims.source_locator: NDSS 2015 version: §I.A and Figure 1, PDF p. 2; §I.B (mixed protocols and automated generation), p. 3; references [35] and [44], p. 14
claims.limitations: conversion costs can dominate a poor partition; security properties are configuration-specific rather than inherited by the framework name

claims.paper_title: Efficient Constant Round Multi-Party Computation Combining BMR and SPDZ
claims.title: SPDZ preprocessing makes BMR garbling actively secure with a two-round online phase
claims.statement: Lindell, Pinkas, Smart, and Yanai use actively secure arithmetic MPC to prepare a BMR garbled circuit, obtaining malicious dishonest-majority MPC whose online phase takes two rounds and is dominated by local garbled-circuit evaluation.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and Sections 3–4
claims.limitations: offline preparation remains substantial; the two-round claim concerns the online phase rather than total execution

claims.paper_title: Two Halves Make a Whole: Reducing Data Transfer in Garbled Circuits Using Half Gates
claims.title: Half-gates reduce each Free-XOR-compatible AND gate to two ciphertexts
claims.statement: Half-gates decomposes a garbled AND into evaluator and garbler halves, reaching two ciphertexts per AND gate while remaining compatible with the Free-XOR wire-label invariant.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and half-gates construction
claims.limitations: the bound is per AND gate rather than end-to-end cost; assumes the stated garbling and hash model

claims.paper_title: MASCOT: Faster Malicious Arithmetic Secure Computation with Oblivious Transfer
claims.title: OT-based checks replace public-key-heavy SPDZ triple generation
claims.statement: MASCOT generates actively secure authenticated arithmetic triples from oblivious transfer, multiplication, and consistency checks, replacing SPDZ's somewhat-homomorphic-encryption preprocessing while preserving its online sharing protocol.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2016/505 (PDF generated 2016-09-14), §1.1 (pp. 3–4), §1.2 (pp. 4–5), §2 and §2.1 (pp. 7–8), §3 Protocol 1 and Theorem 1 (pp. 8–10), §4 and Theorem 2 (pp. 10–16), §5 Protocol 4, Theorem 3 and Corollary 1 (pp. 16–19), §6 Theorems 4–5 and Protocol 6 (pp. 19–21), §7.1 Table 2 (pp. 22–23); PDF page numbers match printed pages
claims.limitations: Preprocessing and checks remain nontrivial; triple communication is n(n − 1)(τλk + (τ + 5)k²) bits (§7.1, p. 22).; Performance figures depend on the OT-extension implementation and network context; Table 1 compares against earlier SPDZ implementations, not a context-independent baseline.

claims.paper_title: Faster Secure Two-Party Computation in the Single-Execution Setting
claims.title: Single-execution malicious garbled 2PC reduces setup and circuit-processing cost
claims.statement: Wang, Malozemoff, and Katz optimize malicious garbled-circuit two-party computation for a single execution by reducing public-key work and improving oblivious-transfer and circuit-processing bottlenecks, with an open implementation supporting the evaluation.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and contribution summary
claims.limitations: performance is tied to the reported implementation context; the contribution does not represent every protocol exposed by later EMP repositories

claims.paper_title: ABY3: A Mixed Protocol Framework for Machine Learning
claims.title: Replicated ring sharing extends mixed-domain computation to three parties
claims.statement: ABY3 constructs a three-party mixed-protocol framework from replicated ring sharing and explicit arithmetic, binary, and Yao-style conversions, with the passive configuration separated from stronger variants.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and protocol overview
claims.limitations: passive and stronger configurations must not be conflated; application-specific fixed-point semantics require separate accounting

claims.paper_title: Efficient Pseudorandom Correlation Generators: Silent OT Extension and More
claims.title: Pseudorandom correlation generators move large OT batches to local seed expansion
claims.statement: Boyle, Couteau, Gilboa, Ishai, Kohl, and Scholl formalize pseudorandom correlation generators and construct silent OT-style expansion, replacing communication and stored correlated randomness with short seeds and local computation.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; PCG definition and constructions
claims.limitations: construction security depends on stated assumptions; local computation and seed-establishment costs remain

claims.paper_title: MOTION — A Framework for Mixed-Protocol Multi-Party Computation
claims.title: MOTION generalizes modular mixed-protocol execution beyond two parties
claims.statement: MOTION provides an asynchronous modular software architecture that combines multiple sharing protocols and conversions for two or more parties under full-threshold passive security.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and framework architecture
claims.limitations: active security is outside the normalized configuration; the paper contribution is distinct from later repository versions

claims.paper_title: MP-SPDZ: A Versatile Framework for Multi-Party Computation
claims.title: MP-SPDZ unifies many MPC backends behind one compiler and virtual machine
claims.statement: MP-SPDZ provides a high-level compiler and virtual-machine architecture that realizes multiple arithmetic and binary MPC protocol families while keeping backend selection and protocol-specific costs explicit.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; architecture and supported-protocol sections
claims.limitations: supported configurations have incompatible security and preprocessing contracts; measurements remain version and environment specific

claims.paper_title: Lightweight Techniques for Private Heavy Hitters
claims.title: Incremental distributed point functions share one non-zero tree path with keys linear in the input length
claims.statement: An incremental DPF secret-shares, between two servers, the values on the nodes of a depth-n binary tree whose only non-zero nodes lie on one root-to-leaf path. BBCGI21 construct one from a pseudorandom generator with key size λ + (λ+2)n + Σ_j ⌈log|G_j|⌉ bits and evaluation on an ℓ-bit prefix costing Σ_{i≤ℓ} (1 + ⌈log|G_i|/λ⌉) PRG calls (Proposition 1), whereas one standard DPF per tree level gives key size and all-prefix evaluation quadratic in n (§6).
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2021/017 (2023-03-23 revision), §5.2 'New tool: Incremental DPF', PDF p. 10; §6, Table 6 and Proposition 1, PDF pp. 11-12; Appendix C.1 definition, PDF p. 17; Appendix C.3 proof of Proposition 1, PDF pp. 18-19; §1 limitation on k servers, PDF p. 3
claims.limitations: The paper states that extending the approach to k servers with k − 1 malicious would need better multiparty DPFs or a different approach (§1, PDF p. 3).; The mechanism gives privacy of client keys only; protection against malformed client keys comes from the separate sketching check and the extractability analysis.

claims.paper_title: Lightweight Techniques for Private Heavy Hitters
claims.title: Two-server check that shared client vectors have weight at most one, private against a malicious server
claims.statement: Two servers holding additive shares of a client vector in F^m check that it is a 0/1 vector with at most one non-zero entry, keeping client privacy against one malicious server up to additive attacks (Proposition 2) and without extra servers or extra client interaction. The client also shares the vector scaled by a secret random κ ∈ F together with correlated randomness; the servers take three inner products with a random sketch vector and evaluate a degree-2 check in two rounds of 4 log|F| bits per server, and an invalid vector is accepted with probability at most 2/|F| (Claim C.1).
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2021/017 (2023-03-23 revision), §4.1, PDF p. 6; §4.2 'New tool: Malicious-secure sketching', PDF pp. 6-7; Appendix C.4 protocol, Claim C.1 and Proposition 2, PDF pp. 19-21; §2.3 remark on correctness, PDF p. 4
claims.limitations: Correctness of the output against a malicious server is not provided (§2.3, PDF p. 4).; Poplar's implementation uses a slightly less efficient variant of the check (§4.2, footnote 1, PDF p. 7).; The check alone does not stop a client whose keys evaluate to one at several points outside the queried set; the paper adds the extractable-DPF analysis for that (§4.1 and §4.3, PDF pp. 6 and 8).

claims.paper_title: Three Halves Make a Whole? Beating the Half-Gates Lower Bound for Garbled Circuits
claims.title: Three-Halves garbles a Free-XOR-compatible AND gate in 1.5λ + 5 bits
claims.statement: RR21 constructs garbling for general Boolean circuits with free XOR gates and 1.5λ + 5 bits per AND gate using slicing and dicing, under the RTCCR hash assumption in Theorem 3. A gate-hiding variant costs 1.5λ + 10 bits per non-free gate; both have leading coefficient 1.5.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2021/749, §1.1 (p. 2), §5.4 Theorem 3 (pp. 18–21), §6.1 (pp. 22–23), §8 (p. 25); PDF page numbers match printed pages
claims.limitations: The 1.5λ term is an upper bound achieved by this construction, not a universal lower bound.; Input encoding, output decoding, OT, and malicious-security enforcement are not included in a per-AND gate size.

claims.paper_title: The Round Complexity of Statistical MPC with Optimal Resiliency
claims.title: Four-round statistical MPC with GOD and exponential depth-dependent work
claims.statement: Every functionality represented by a Boolean circuit of size S and depth D has a four-round statistically secure MPC protocol with GOD against static active rushing unbounded corruption of t < n/2 parties, with error 2^(-κ) and running time polynomial in κ, 2^n, S and 2^D, in the source's secure-channel and broadcast model.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2023/418 revision 2025-06-17, §1 model (p. 5), §1.1.3 and Theorem 1.5 with following discussion and footnote 3 (p. 8)
claims.limitations: This is not polynomial-time MPC for arbitrary polynomial-size circuits or growing n.; The NC¹ efficiency discussion has a qualified extension via secure reductions from log space; it is not a universal impossibility outside NC¹.; No adaptive-corruption or practical-performance claim is admitted.

claims.paper_title: FOLEAGE: F4OLE-Based Multi-Party Computation for Boolean Circuits
claims.title: F4-OLE PCGs give near-linear communication for multiparty Boolean triples
claims.statement: FOLEAGE constructs multiparty Boolean-triple preprocessing from an F4-OLE pseudorandom correlation generator, with communication near linear in the number of parties times the number of triples plus lower-order seed terms.
claims.source_locator: Abstract and construction overview
claims.limitations: lower-order seed costs and local work remain; exact concrete gains depend on party count and implementation context

claims.paper_title: High-Throughput Secure Multiparty Computation with an Honest Majority in Various Network Settings
claims.title: Topology-aware Trio and Quad tolerate all but two low-bandwidth links
claims.statement: HP-MPC redistributes Trio and Quad communication so all but two links may have arbitrarily low bandwidth and all but one may have arbitrarily high latency, without increasing the protocols' total per-multiplication communication.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; Contributions; heterogeneous-network protocol variants
claims.limitations: security and message schedules differ between Trio and Quad; the weak-link claim is protocol-structural rather than a portable throughput number; disconnection and availability are not implied

claims.paper_title: High-Throughput Secure Multiparty Computation with an Honest Majority in Various Network Settings
claims.title: Trio and Quad reduce per-gate local arithmetic without extra communication
claims.statement: By reducing correlations among party shares, Trio and Quad require up to half as many basic local instructions per gate as the paper's related baselines while retaining total communication of three and five ring elements per multiplication.
claims.source_locator: Abstract; Contributions; protocol operation counts in Tables 1 and 13
claims.limitations: the up-to-half comparison is operation- and baseline-specific; wall-clock gains depend on implementation and workload; Trio and Quad have different security contracts

claims.paper_title: High-Throughput Secure Multiparty Computation with an Honest Majority in Various Network Settings
claims.title: Trio and Quad use masked sharing at three and four parties
claims.statement: HP-MPC constructs Trio, a three-party protocol with one passive corruption, and Quad, a four-party protocol with one malicious corruption, using paper-specific masked-sharing semantics and total communication of three and five ring elements per multiplication respectively.
claims.source_locator: Contributions; Sections 3–5; Trio and Quad multiplication protocols
claims.limitations: the two configurations do not share one adversary contract; setup uses shared-key pseudorandom generation; communication totals do not by themselves imply the reported throughput

claims.paper_title: Statistical MPC with a Constant Communication Overhead
claims.title: Statistical GOD with constant communication overhead across Θ(n^7) SIMD evaluations
claims.statement: With n = 3t+1 and synchronous private authenticated channels, the current CDPP manuscript gives statistically secure MPC with GOD and O(D) expected rounds against malicious adaptive unbounded corruption; for Θ(n^7) parallel evaluations of a circuit with c_M multiplication gates, one field-element input per party and one common output, total communication is O(c_M n^7+n^8) field elements.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2025/1555 revision 2026-05-22, §1 adversary model (p. 1), §1.1 Theorem 1.1 (p. 2), §3 field/network convention (p. 11), §7 Theorem 7.1 and footnotes 9–10 (pp. 23–24)
claims.limitations: O(D) is an expected round bound, not a deterministic worst-case bound.; General-circuit-to-SIMD compilation introduces a log |C| size factor and potentially a depth-dependent additive term for irregular circuits.; The current revision is synchronous; an older abstract's asynchronous claims are not admitted.; No constant local-computation overhead or measured practicality claim is admitted.

claims.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Garbled Circuits from Shannon-Type Information Inequalities
claims.title: A 1.5λ lower bound for strongly secure Free-XOR AND gates with restricted evaluator queries
claims.statement: JRR25 Theorem 26 gives a 1.5λ − negl(λ) garbled-gate size lower bound for the class of AND gates with input/output bit flips, under Definition 12 input-to-output syntax, λ-bit labels with the common Free-XOR offset, Definition 16 strong security, and non-adaptive coordinated evaluator queries to the random oracle.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2025/876, §1.1 (pp. 3–4), Definitions 12–14 (pp. 9–10), §3.3 and Definition 16 (pp. 11–12), Theorem 26 and Corollary 27 (p. 23); PDF page numbers match printed pages
claims.limitations: Does not cover adaptive or uncoordinated evaluator oracle queries.; Does not establish a whole-circuit lower bound for non-projective or layer-batched encodings.; Strong security is not silently replaced by ordinary garbling security.

claims.paper_title: Actively Secure MPC with O(|C|) Computation and Communication via CRT
claims.title: Active CRT-based MPC keeps leading computation and communication linear with abort
claims.statement: For any fixed 0 < ε < 1/2 and fields with log |F| = Ω(n² log n), BEP gives statistically secure MPC with abort for general arithmetic circuits against t < (1/2−ε)n active corruptions, with O(|C| log |F|) leading communication and bit-computation cost under the source convention suppressing statistical-security, log n and log log |F| factors.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2026/1270, §1.1 Theorem 1 and footnotes 3–4 (p. 2), preceding GOD discussion (p. 2) and §1.2 (p. 3)
claims.limitations: Guaranteed output delivery is not provided.; No small-field, adaptive-corruption or exact O(D)-round claim is normalized from this introductory theorem.; Constant overhead with guaranteed output delivery for a single general circuit is not claimed.

claims.paper_title: Suffix-Invariant Programmable PRFs and Applications to Stacked Garbling
claims.title: Stacked garbling whose input-routing cost no longer scales with branches times input length
claims.statement: GHJY26 Theorem 10 gives a garbling scheme from black-box one-way functions that selects one of B = 2^n = poly(λ) Boolean branches of size C with a common I-bit input, with total garbled size O(I log B·λ + Bλ + Cλ) bits and O(B log B) garbler and evaluator time, and the same correctness and security guarantees as LogStack, whose garbled size is O(BIλ + Cλ). The demultiplexer is a garbled programmer for a short-key offline-online suffix-invariant programmable PRF (Theorem 8 and Lemma 3).
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2026/815 (2026-07-02 revision), §1.1 Theorem 1 (informal) and concrete comparison, PDF p. 5; Theorem 2 (informal), PDF p. 6; §2.3 suffix invariance and garbage collection, PDF p. 11; §6.2 Theorem 8 and Lemma 3, PDF p. 26; §7.1 Theorem 9, PDF pp. 30–31; §7.2 Theorem 10, PDF p. 33; Appendix E Theorem 14, PDF p. 54. PDF pages are printed pages plus three.
claims.limitations: The circuit term O(Cλ) is inherited from the base Yao scheme (point-and-permute, or free XOR and half gates under a circular correlation-robust hash; Appendix E, PDF p. 53); the result does not bear on the single-gate question MPC-OP-016.; No implementation or measurement is reported.; The suffix-invariant programmable PRF, the adaptive programmable PRF from one-way functions (§5.4), and the PRF/DPF equivalences (Theorems 4–6) are not recorded as separate contributions.

claims.paper_title: Compressing Correlations via Secret Replication: PCFs from Symmetric Cryptography
claims.title: PRF-based multiparty scalar-vector triples with exponential party-dependent key cost
claims.statement: IKR construct a k-party PCF for additive shares of a scalar x, vector a, and xa using only PRFs; if each scalar share lies in a common support S, each party holds k|S|^(k−1)−(k−1)|S|^(k−2)+2k−2 PRF keys and evaluates each key once per coordinate.
claims.source_locator: ITC 2026 proceedings, Theorem 2, p. 7:6; Definition 6, pp. 7:8–7:9; §4.2 and Corollary 27, pp. 7:14–7:17; Definitions 12–13, pp. 7:10–7:11
claims.limitations: Exponential dependence on k remains even when F=S=F2.; Adaptive evaluation indices do not establish adaptive party corruption, malicious distributed key generation, or UC composition.; This atom is unauthenticated SVMT; authenticated variants have additional parameters and are not folded into its guarantee.

claims.paper_title: Compressing Correlations via Secret Replication: PCFs from Symmetric Cryptography
claims.title: Secret projection recovers small-scalar VOLE PCFs from PRFs
claims.statement: IKR derive a two-party PCF for VOLE over a finite field F with scalar in X subset F from any PRF; the direct construction assigns |X| keys to the sender and |X|−1 to the receiver, with one PRF call per held key per evaluated coordinate.
claims.source_locator: ITC 2026 proceedings, Theorem 1, p. 7:5; Corollary 22 and Remarks 24–25, p. 7:14; Definitions 12–13, pp. 7:10–7:11
claims.limitations: Large scalar domains make the direct evaluation expensive; key compression alone does not remove this evaluation cost.; No generic OWF-based random-OT PCG or complete malicious MPC protocol is established by this contribution.

claims.paper_title: Breaking the Ω(|C|κ) Barrier on Garbled Circuit Size in the Random Oracle Model
claims.title: Layer-batched ROM garbling separates circuit-size cost from statistical error
claims.statement: LS26 Theorem 1 gives Boolean-circuit garbling of size O(|C| log T + Dκ² log T) bits and input encoding O(WI log T) bits in the programmable random-oracle model, with error 2^(−κ) against a computationally unbounded T-query adversary; D is depth and WI is the number of input wires.
claims.source_locator: ePrint 2026/1297, §1.1 Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 (pp. 4–5), §1.2 (pp. 7–8), §3.4 Definition 1 (pp. 16–17); PDF page numbers match printed pages
claims.limitations: The work explicitly defers improved concrete size; no measured implementation advantage is claimed here.; The input-encoding term remains separate and is not omitted from full communication accounting.; This different interface is not an APPROACHES edge to the single-gate question MPC-OP-016.

threads.label: Garbling and distributed garbling
threads.description: Garbled-circuit evaluation from two-party foundations through multiparty and gate optimizations.

threads.label: Boolean sharing and OT
threads.description: Boolean secret sharing, oblivious transfer, and OT-amplified protocols.

threads.label: Arithmetic sharing and LSSS
threads.description: Arithmetic secret sharing and multiplicative linear-secret-sharing architectures.

threads.label: Authenticated-share MPC
threads.description: Authenticated shares, bits, and preprocessing for active security.

threads.label: Correlation generation
threads.description: Triples, OT extension, PCGs, and other reusable offline correlations.

threads.label: Mixed-domain compilation
threads.description: Conversions and compilers across arithmetic, Boolean, and garbled representations.

threads.label: Security compilation and simulation
threads.description: Security compilers, transcript-simulation mechanisms, and composition contracts across protocol environments.

problems.label: Generality and feasibility
problems.question: Which functionalities, corruption thresholds, access structures, and forms of composition can general secure computation achieve?

problems.label: Active security
problems.question: How are malicious deviations detected or tolerated across arithmetic, Boolean, and garbled protocols?

problems.label: Adaptive and proactive security
problems.question: How can MPC remain secure when corruption timing changes or shares must be refreshed over time?

problems.label: Rounds and communication
problems.question: Which results reduce or bound the rounds and communication that secure computation needs, including the size of a garbled gate?

problems.label: Network and delivery
problems.question: Which results weaken the network a protocol assumes, from synchronous private channels to asynchronous or insecure links, and what output delivery remains?

problems.label: Setup and preprocessing
problems.question: Which results change the setup a protocol relies on, from correlated randomness supplied by a trusted dealer to preprocessing the parties generate themselves?

MPC-CONTRIB-1982-YAO-2PC.label: Two-party SFE
MPC-CONTRIB-1982-YAO-2PC.selection_rationale: Establishes secure two-party function evaluation as the task boundary needed to understand every later garbling and 2PC optimization without crediting it with all modern garbled-circuit details.
MPC-CONTRIB-1982-YAO-2PC.lane_rationale: The card isolates private two-party function evaluation as a general research task and its feasibility boundary; it does not claim all later garbled-circuit machinery.

MPC-CONTRIB-1987-GMW-COMPILER.label: General MPC compiler
MPC-CONTRIB-1987-GMW-COMPILER.selection_rationale: Supplies the general circuit-to-MPC compiler and separates passive evaluation from adversary enforcement, a contract later sharing and authentication mechanisms deliberately instantiate.
MPC-CONTRIB-1987-GMW-COMPILER.lane_rationale: The principal delta is the concrete circuit-to-MPC compilation architecture and adversary-enforcement transforms, not merely the historical fact of general feasibility.

MPC-CONTRIB-1988-BGW-THRESHOLDS.label: MPC threshold frontier
MPC-CONTRIB-1988-BGW-THRESHOLDS.selection_rationale: Fixes the unconditional honest-majority corruption thresholds and the arithmetic-sharing architecture that later threshold, network, and access-structure results must qualify.
MPC-CONTRIB-1988-BGW-THRESHOLDS.lane_rationale: The mapped claim characterizes information-theoretic MPC feasibility and matching corruption-threshold limitations in the specified synchronous private-channel model.

MPC-CONTRIB-1990-BMR-CONSTANT.label: Constant-round BMR
MPC-CONTRIB-1990-BMR-CONSTANT.selection_rationale: Shows that distributed garbling can remove circuit depth from online round complexity, anchoring the BMR line later combined with active arithmetic preprocessing.
MPC-CONTRIB-1990-BMR-CONSTANT.lane_rationale: The node's named delta removes circuit depth from communication-round complexity through distributed garbling; constant rounds do not mean constant communication.

MPC-CONTRIB-1991-BEAVER-TRIPLES.label: Beaver triples
MPC-CONTRIB-1991-BEAVER-TRIPLES.selection_rationale: Isolates input-independent multiplication correlations as the online/offline interface reused by SPDZ and later preprocessing replacements.
MPC-CONTRIB-1991-BEAVER-TRIPLES.lane_rationale: The contribution supplies a reusable input-independent multiplication-correlation mechanism for masking online products; it is not a complete preprocessing implementation or a standalone benchmark.

MPC-CONTRIB-1993-ASYNC-FEASIBILITY.label: Asynchronous MPC
MPC-CONTRIB-1993-ASYNC-FEASIBILITY.selection_rationale: Introduces asynchronous verifiable sharing and agreement with distinct optimal fail-stop and Byzantine bounds; omitting the node would collapse two fault models into a generic honest-majority label.
MPC-CONTRIB-1993-ASYNC-FEASIBILITY.lane_rationale: The card establishes general asynchronous MPC feasibility with distinct optimal fail-stop and Byzantine resilience bounds; the fault models and errorless-computation conditions remain explicit.

MPC-CONTRIB-1996-ADAPTIVE-NCE.label: Adaptive corruption security
MPC-CONTRIB-1996-ADAPTIVE-NCE.selection_rationale: Keeps non-committing encryption visible as the insecure-channel simulation mechanism for non-erasing adaptive corruption, preventing it from being conflated with epoch-based share refresh.
MPC-CONTRIB-1996-ADAPTIVE-NCE.lane_rationale: The claim is a non-committing-encryption transformation realizing adaptive security over insecure channels for non-erasing parties under stated thresholds, not an independent security analysis alone.

MPC-CONTRIB-2000-CDM-LSSS.label: Multiplicative LSSS MPC
MPC-CONTRIB-2000-CDM-LSSS.selection_rationale: Generalizes threshold polynomial sharing to multiplicative LSSS access structures, making the sharing representation an explicit compiler interface.
MPC-CONTRIB-2000-CDM-LSSS.lane_rationale: The contribution constructs MPC through a multiplicative-LSSS interface supporting qualified general access structures; its principal role is a reusable construction architecture.

MPC-CONTRIB-2001-UC-COMPOSITION.label: UC composition contract
MPC-CONTRIB-2001-UC-COMPOSITION.selection_rationale: Keeps composability visible as a security-framework contribution so protocol rows do not silently inherit concurrent composition from stand-alone simulation.
MPC-CONTRIB-2001-UC-COMPOSITION.lane_rationale: The work defines environment-based universally composable security and establishes the composition theorem; protocol implementations do not inherit this framework without meeting its hypotheses.

MPC-CONTRIB-2003-IKNP-OTEXT.label: IKNP OT extension
MPC-CONTRIB-2003-IKNP-OTEXT.selection_rationale: Establishes symmetric-key expansion of a small base-OT seed, the practical correlation mechanism consumed by later Boolean active-security protocols.
MPC-CONTRIB-2003-IKNP-OTEXT.lane_rationale: The source claim explicitly reduces public-key work for an OT batch to a small base-OT seed followed by symmetric-key expansion; the improved resource is public-key computation, not zero communication.

MPC-CONTRIB-2008-FREEXOR.label: Free-XOR
MPC-CONTRIB-2008-FREEXOR.selection_rationale: Changes the garbling invariant so XOR gates disappear from the ciphertext and cryptographic-operation budget, redefining the field's concrete circuit cost metric.
MPC-CONTRIB-2008-FREEXOR.lane_rationale: The global wire-label offset eliminates ciphertexts and cryptographic operations specifically for XOR gates while leaving nonlinear-gate cost and correlation assumptions intact.

MPC-CONTRIB-2009-PRACTICAL2PC.label: Practical 2PC codesign
MPC-CONTRIB-2009-PRACTICAL2PC.selection_rationale: Represents the whole-stack semi-honest 2PC co-design transition without confusing an implementation-aware research delta with a mutable artifact or one benchmark run.
MPC-CONTRIB-2009-PRACTICAL2PC.lane_rationale: The card records implementation-aware coordination of circuit generation, garbling, OT, memory, and networking for end-to-end semi-honest 2PC; performance remains tied to the paper's workloads and implementation.

MPC-CONTRIB-2011-SPDZ-AUTH.label: Authenticated-share MPC
MPC-CONTRIB-2011-SPDZ-AUTH.selection_rationale: Establishes authenticated arithmetic sharing with a light actively secure dishonest-majority online phase, the stable interface later preprocessing work deliberately preserves.
MPC-CONTRIB-2011-SPDZ-AUTH.lane_rationale: SPDZ supplies an authenticated-arithmetic-sharing architecture with global-MAC checks and an explicit preprocessing/online interface; stronger active-security guarantees qualify the construction rather than create a separate lane.

MPC-CONTRIB-2012-TINYOT-AUTHBITS.label: TinyOT authenticated bits
MPC-CONTRIB-2012-TINYOT-AUTHBITS.selection_rationale: Gives a Boolean-sharing active-security architecture based on authenticated bits and OT preprocessing rather than treating generic compilers or garbled cut-and-choose as the only route.
MPC-CONTRIB-2012-TINYOT-AUTHBITS.lane_rationale: TinyOT gives a specialized actively secure Boolean 2PC protocol from authenticated bits, OT preprocessing, and consistency checks; the node identifies how that security contract is realized.

MPC-CONTRIB-2015-ABY-MIXED.label: ABY mixed protocols
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-ABY-MIXED.selection_rationale: Makes arithmetic, Boolean, and garbled domains explicit typed choices connected by costed conversions, anchoring mixed-protocol compilation rather than a single sharing family.
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-ABY-MIXED.lane_rationale: The primary contribution is the mixed-domain framework and concrete conversion protocols among arithmetic sharing, Boolean sharing, and Yao garbling, not a single cross-work performance ranking.

MPC-CONTRIB-2015-BMR-SPDZ.label: BMR + SPDZ
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-BMR-SPDZ.selection_rationale: Preserves the cross-architecture composition of SPDZ preprocessing and BMR evaluation as reviewed-related, since it changes how components combine without starting a broader default thread.
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-BMR-SPDZ.lane_rationale: The node composes an actively secure arithmetic preprocessing engine with distributed BMR garbling to realize a dishonest-majority protocol; the two-round claim is limited to its online phase.

MPC-CONTRIB-2015-HALFGATES.label: Half-gates
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-HALFGATES.selection_rationale: Marks the two-ciphertext Free-XOR-compatible AND construction, the concrete nonlinear-gate communication point used by modern garbled-circuit implementations.
MPC-CONTRIB-2015-HALFGATES.lane_rationale: The principal delta is two ciphertexts per garbled AND while preserving the Free-XOR invariant; this is a specific nonlinear-gate communication improvement.

MPC-CONTRIB-2016-MASCOT-TRIPLES.label: MASCOT triples
MPC-CONTRIB-2016-MASCOT-TRIPLES.selection_rationale: Replaces SPDZ's public-key-heavy offline generator with OT-based authenticated triples while preserving the online protocol, making backend modularity historically visible.
MPC-CONTRIB-2016-MASCOT-TRIPLES.lane_rationale: The mapped statement specifies an OT-based authenticated-triple generator replacing SHE preprocessing while retaining the SPDZ online interface; it does not normalize a context-independent performance advantage.

MPC-CONTRIB-2018-ABY3-REPLICATED.label: ABY3 replicated sharing
MPC-CONTRIB-2018-ABY3-REPLICATED.selection_rationale: Moves mixed-domain computation to a three-party replicated-ring design, changing party model, sharing representation, and conversion costs together.
MPC-CONTRIB-2018-ABY3-REPLICATED.lane_rationale: The claim gives a three-party replicated-ring architecture and domain conversions; changing the party/trust contract is not an unconditional improvement over two-party ABY.

MPC-CONTRIB-2019-PCG-SILENT.label: Silent PCG correlations
MPC-CONTRIB-2019-PCG-SILENT.selection_rationale: Defines seed-expanded pseudorandom correlations and the silent-OT branch, changing large-batch correlation cost from communication and storage toward local computation.
MPC-CONTRIB-2019-PCG-SILENT.lane_rationale: The card explicitly isolates the new seed-to-correlation abstraction and its feasibility through silent expansion: compact correlated seeds define an independently reusable primitive, while local-work and setup costs remain.

MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MOTION-MULTIPARTY.label: MOTION framework
MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MOTION-MULTIPARTY.selection_rationale: Represents a modular multiparty mixed-protocol runtime as a systems-architecture contribution while leaving its pinned artifact and exact passive configurations separate.
MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MOTION-MULTIPARTY.lane_rationale: The card contains a modular mixed-protocol execution architecture with explicit gate, wire, conversion, and runtime interfaces for passive multiparty computation; this is more than an artifact release and is not itself an asynchronous-network security theorem.

MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MPSPDZ-FRAMEWORK.label: MP-SPDZ framework
MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MPSPDZ-FRAMEWORK.selection_rationale: Establishes one compiler and virtual-machine surface across many explicit MPC backends, providing a practice anchor without implying that their security or cost contracts are interchangeable.
MPC-CONTRIB-2020-MPSPDZ-FRAMEWORK.lane_rationale: The contribution is a high-level compiler and virtual-machine architecture decoupling programs from explicit arithmetic and binary protocol backends; it is not merely repository availability or benchmark publication.

MPC-CONTRIB-2021-THREE-HALVES.label: Three-Halves garbling
MPC-CONTRIB-2021-THREE-HALVES.selection_rationale: Continues the Free-XOR garbling line past the half-gates point by leaving the linear-garbling model while keeping the global offset, and supplies the upper-bound reference for the garbled AND-gate size question.
MPC-CONTRIB-2021-THREE-HALVES.lane_rationale: The principal delta is 1.5λ + 5 bits per Free-XOR-compatible AND gate under the RTCCR assumption; it is a per-gate upper bound, not a lower bound or an end-to-end protocol cost.

MPC-CONTRIB-2024-FOLEAGE-F4.label: FOLEAGE preprocessing
MPC-CONTRIB-2024-FOLEAGE-F4.selection_rationale: Advances the PCG line to near-linear multiparty Boolean-triple communication through an F4-OLE construction, preserving its protocol optimization identity despite implementation evidence.
MPC-CONTRIB-2024-FOLEAGE-F4.lane_rationale: The mapped delta is near-linear party-by-triple preprocessing communication using F4-OLE PCG machinery, with seed terms and local computation explicitly retained.

MPC-CONTRIB-2025-JRR-FREE-XOR-BOUND.label: Garbled-gate lower bound
MPC-CONTRIB-2025-JRR-FREE-XOR-BOUND.selection_rationale: Records the 1.5λ lower bound that matches the leading Three-Halves cost for strongly secure Free-XOR AND gates, so that cost reads as optimal only inside the restricted evaluator-query model.
MPC-CONTRIB-2025-JRR-FREE-XOR-BOUND.lane_rationale: A lower bound is Foundation; Theorem 26 bounds strongly secure Free-XOR AND gates under non-adaptive coordinated evaluator queries and is not a whole-circuit or unrestricted-query bound.

reading_collections.label: Definitions, feasibility, and composition
reading_collections.question: What does security mean for MPC, and which guarantees are possible under which corruption, network, setup, and composition conditions?
reading_collections.includes: Security definitions and the simulation paradigm, composition frameworks, general feasibility and impossibility results, fairness and output guarantees, and adaptive or mobile corruption models, read as results about what is possible.
reading_collections.excludes: The security level of a concrete protocol is a filter on the comparison page, not membership here; protocols that realize a feasibility result are read in their own subfields.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers early two-party and multiparty feasibility, universal composability, non-committing encryption for adaptive security, and fairness without an honest majority. Round complexity of computational MPC and later impossibility results are not yet recorded.

members.reason: The contribution establishes private function evaluation as a general research task through early two-party protocols, without attributing modern simulation definitions or later garbled-circuit constructions to this atomic record.

General circuit compilation and the separation of passive evaluation from stronger adversary enforcement directly establish a generality and security-compilation boundary, rather than merely recording the security properties of one optimized gate protocol.

Environment-based simulation, ideal-functionality replacement, and the universal composition theorem are the direct research objects, with the framework and setup assumptions retained rather than inferred from a protocol's UC label.

Non-committing encryption supplies an adaptive-simulation transformation for non-erasing parties over insecure channels under the stated trapdoor assumptions; the principal construction handles fewer than one third corruptions and the card separately notes a modification below one half, not an epoch-based refresh guarantee.

The result gives complete fairness for n-party Boolean OR and three-party majority with any t<n corruptions under the stated cryptographic and private-broadcast-or-PKI conditions, including a super-logarithmic round lower bound for majority; it is not a generic fairness or guaranteed-output-delivery upgrade.
The honest-majority thresholds are a feasibility characterization; the protocols themselves are read in the honest-majority subfield.
Feasibility of general MPC with arbitrarily delayed messages is a model result; the asynchronous protocol is read in the honest-majority subfield.
Mobile corruptions are a corruption model; the share-refresh protocols are read in the honest-majority subfield.

reading_collections.label: Honest-majority and information-theoretic MPC
reading_collections.question: How efficiently can parties compute with secret sharing when a minority is corrupt, in rounds, communication, and computation, with or without computational assumptions?
reading_collections.includes: Threshold and linear-secret-sharing protocols for t < n/2 or t < n/3, information-theoretic and statistical MPC, asynchronous and proactive variants, the round and communication complexity of these protocols, and high-throughput honest-majority protocols for few parties.
reading_collections.excludes: Dishonest-majority protocols, including SPDZ-style authenticated sharing, are read in their own subfield; general feasibility theorems are read in the foundations subfield.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers BGW, linear secret sharing, asynchronous and proactive protocols, recent round and communication results, and three- and four-party high-throughput protocols. Packed secret sharing and hyper-invertible matrices are not yet recorded.

members.reason: The contribution's own construction combines polynomial sharing, degree reduction, and verifiable sharing for general arithmetic evaluation, while preserving distinct model-specific passive and active threshold results.

Multiplicative linear secret sharing supplies a representation-level interface for shared evaluation beyond a single threshold, subject to the stated multiplication and robustness conditions rather than applying to every LSSS.

The atomic construction combines asynchronous verifiable sharing, agreement, and online error correction rather than merely tagging a protocol as asynchronous; its fail-stop and Byzantine resilience bounds remain distinct.

Cross-epoch rerandomization and erasure directly change maintenance of distributed shares without changing the protected secret; the mechanism retains its per-epoch assumptions and is not a complete MPC protocol.

The protocol achieves four-round statistical MPC with guaranteed output delivery for t < n/2, with work exponential in depth; it directly advances the round complexity of honest-majority information-theoretic MPC.

The protocol reaches constant communication overhead for statistical MPC with guaranteed output delivery across many parallel evaluations, a direct communication result in honest-majority information-theoretic MPC.
The protocol keeps leading computation and communication linear in circuit size for t < (1/2 − ε)n with abort, a direct efficiency result for honest-majority MPC.
Trio and Quad change masked-share layouts, multiplication, and checking rules in their respective three- and four-party protocols, retaining their distinct passive and malicious security contracts.

Revised masked-share correlations reduce local instructions on the multiplication path without extra communicated ring elements, a protocol-level efficiency delta rather than a new resource generator or universal benchmark ranking.

Topology-aware message schedules directly change execution of the specified sharing protocols while retaining their per-multiplication communication totals; the result is not general asynchronous feasibility, availability, or portable throughput.
Circuit randomization is also used inside honest-majority protocols; the preprocessing paradigm itself is read in the dishonest-majority subfield.
Replicated three-party sharing is an honest-majority protocol; its typed conversions are read in the compilers subfield.

reading_collections.label: Dishonest-majority MPC
reading_collections.question: How can parties compute securely when all but one may be corrupt, using preprocessing, authenticated secret sharing, or homomorphic encryption?
reading_collections.includes: The preprocessing paradigm with multiplication triples, authenticated arithmetic and Boolean sharing such as SPDZ, BDOZ, and TinyOT, OT-based and HE-based offline phases, and HE-based MPC.
reading_collections.excludes: How oblivious transfer and correlations are generated is read in the correlation-generation subfield; garbled-circuit protocols are read in the garbled-circuits subfield.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers circuit randomization, SPDZ, TinyOT, and MASCOT, with a client-aided two-server validity check from private aggregation read as context. Overdrive, Le Mans, and threshold-FHE MPC are not yet recorded as results.

members.reason: The atomic mechanism uses input-independent multiplicative correlations to separate online arithmetic from offline preparation, directly defining the resource abstraction rather than a particular generator.
The contribution preprocesses authenticated multiplication correlations and establishes the global-MAC invariant used by online arithmetic, directly changing the authenticated-resource construction.
The card constructs OT-generated authenticated bits and AND correlations with tailored consistency checks, directly advancing Boolean preprocessing resources.
OT-based product generation, authentication, sacrifice, and consistency checks replace the original homomorphic-encryption triple generator while preserving the SPDZ online interface.
GMW's secret-sharing protocol with oblivious transfer is the dishonest-majority baseline; its general compilation result is read in the foundations subfield.
OT extension supplies the oblivious transfers that OT-based preprocessing consumes; the extension mechanism is read in the correlation-generation subfield.
Silent correlation generation can supply preprocessing for dishonest-majority protocols; the generator is read in the correlation-generation subfield.
The construction uses SPDZ-style preprocessing to prepare distributed garbling; the garbling protocol is read in the garbled-circuits subfield.

With two servers of which one may be malicious, the check keeps client privacy by borrowing an authenticated scaled-copy encoding and Beaver-style correlated randomness supplied by the client; it is a special-purpose validity check inside private aggregation, not a general-purpose dishonest-majority protocol.

reading_collections.label: Garbled circuits
reading_collections.question: How are circuits garbled and evaluated, how small can garbled gates be, and how are garbled protocols made secure against malicious parties?
reading_collections.includes: Garbling schemes and their gate size, multiparty garbling (BMR), lower bounds, and constant-round or malicious two-party and multiparty execution built on garbling.
reading_collections.excludes: Garbling is not a synonym for two-party computation; independent OT generation and mixed-protocol conversion are read in their own subfields.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers BMR, free XOR, half gates, three halves, a lower bound for strongly secure gates, practical semi-honest 2PC, single-execution malicious 2PC, BMR with SPDZ preprocessing, layer-batched garbling, and stacked garbling for conditional branching with a programmable-PRF demultiplexer. Cut-and-choose and authenticated garbling are not yet recorded as results, nor are the earlier stacked-garbling schemes (Heath–Kolesnikov 2020, LogStack 2021).

members.reason: Distributed garbling changes the execution architecture so interaction rounds no longer grow with circuit depth; the contribution does not claim constant communication or computation.
The global wire-label offset directly removes garbled ciphertexts and cryptographic operations for XOR gates under the stated correlation assumptions, without eliminating nonlinear-gate costs.

End-to-end co-design coordinates circuit generation, garbling, OT handling, memory, and networking for semi-honest garbled two-party execution; this is a systems contribution to that path rather than merely an artifact release or invention of its components.
The Free-XOR-compatible AND construction uses two correlated half-gates and two ciphertexts per AND; this directly changes garbling communication without asserting an end-to-end latency improvement.

Protocol and implementation co-design reduces public-key work and circuit-processing costs for single-execution malicious garbled two-party computation; it does not stand for every backend in later EMP repositories.

Authenticated arithmetic computation prepares and checks distributed BMR garbling, directly enabling the specified malicious dishonest-majority execution path; the two-round claim applies only to the online phase.
The construction garbles a Free-XOR-compatible AND gate in about 1.5λ bits, below the two-ciphertext half-gates bound for linear schemes; it is a direct advance in garbled gate size.
The result proves a 1.5λ lower bound for strongly secure Free-XOR AND gates when evaluator queries are restricted, directly bounding garbled gate size.
Layer-batched garbling in the programmable random-oracle model changes the per-gate cost of garbled circuits for wide circuits; it is a direct garbling advance within its stated query bound.

A suffix-invariant programmable-PRF demultiplexer removes the branches-times-input-length term from the garbled size of stacked garbling for conditional branching while keeping LogStack's computation; it is a direct garbled-size advance for branching, not a change in garbled gate size.

The card establishes private two-party function evaluation as a general task, providing conceptual context without attributing a later complete garbled-circuit construction or modern formalization to this record.
OT extension provides background on the cost of a distinct resource used in secure-computation execution; its atomic delta expands OT batches rather than changing garbling encodings or evaluation.

reading_collections.label: Oblivious transfer and correlation generation
reading_collections.question: How are oblivious transfer and other correlations such as VOLE, OLE, and triples constructed, extended, and generated with little communication?
reading_collections.includes: Oblivious transfer constructions and extension, pseudorandom correlation generators and functions, silent OT and VOLE, and triple generation from correlations.
reading_collections.excludes: Using a correlation inside a complete protocol is read in that protocol's subfield; OLE, VOLE, authenticated bits, and triples are not treated as the same functionality.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers IKNP OT extension, silent OT from pseudorandom correlation generators, F4-OLE triples, and correlation functions from PRFs. Base OT constructions and OT completeness results are not yet recorded.

members.reason: The atomic mechanism expands a small base-OT seed into many transfers through symmetric-key matrix expansion, directly changing the cost of the OT interface.
The card explicitly includes silent OT constructions from compact correlated seeds; this OT-specific part directly changes communication and storage without eliminating seed setup or local work.
F4-OLE-based Boolean-triple generation is a neighboring correlation interface that clarifies the boundary of OT; this context does not assert OT use or an OT improvement by FOLEAGE.

The construction gives multiparty scalar-vector triple correlation functions from PRFs, a direct result on generating correlations from symmetric cryptography; its key size grows exponentially with the number of parties.
Secret projection yields pseudorandom correlation functions for small-scalar VOLE from PRFs alone, a direct result on correlation generation from symmetric cryptography.
Multiplication triples are the correlation many generators target; their use in online protocols is read in the dishonest-majority subfield.
Authenticated bits are generated from oblivious transfer; the protocol that consumes them is read in the dishonest-majority subfield.
Triples are generated from OT with consistency checks; the SPDZ-style protocol that consumes them is read in the dishonest-majority subfield.

reading_collections.label: Compilers and mixed-protocol computation
reading_collections.question: How are secure computations programmed, compiled, and executed, and how are subcomputations assigned to and converted between protocols?
reading_collections.includes: Programming tools and compilers, typed conversion between arithmetic, Boolean, and garbled representations, automatic protocol selection, and execution frameworks.
reading_collections.excludes: A tool release or measurement is not a new protocol; security composition theorems are read in the foundations subfield.
reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers TASTY, automatic protocol selection, ABY, ABY3, MOTION, and MP-SPDZ. RAM-based MPC and oblivious data structures are not yet recorded.

members.reason: TASTYL explicitly describes homomorphic and garbled values and their conversions, and TASTY generates the corresponding semi-honest two-party execution. The programmer supplies the protocol representation choices; automatic protocol selection is explicitly left to future work, not claimed by this atom.

Conversion-aware assignment of operations between HE-based arithmetic and garbled circuits is the direct research target, with integer programming and a greedy heuristic evaluated against a specified forecast cost model. Model-relative optimization is not universal fastest execution or a proved hardness result for this partitioning problem.
Explicit, costed conversions let a single computation move among arithmetic sharing, Boolean sharing, and Yao garbling, with the source card's passive two-party configuration conditions retained.

The three-party replicated-ring architecture supplies arithmetic, binary, and Yao-style conversions tailored to that party model, directly changing mixed-domain execution without combining the security claims of all variants.

Modular protocol providers and conversions support mixed execution for two or more parties under the documented passive full-threshold model; asynchronous runtime scheduling does not establish security in an asynchronous network model.
MP-SPDZ puts many MPC protocols behind one compiler and virtual machine; it is a direct contribution to programming tools and execution frameworks, not a new protocol.

Arithmetic preprocessing that prepares distributed garbling supplies a cross-phase composition contrast, not evidence of ABY-style typed conversion among subcomputations within the online computation.

primer.title: Secure multiparty computation
primer.summary: Protocols that let mutually distrusting parties compute a joint function of their private inputs while revealing nothing beyond the output, even when some parties are corrupted.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.content:
In secure multiparty computation (MPC), \(n\) parties holding inputs
\(x_1,\dots,x_n\) run a protocol to compute \(f(x_1,\dots,x_n)\). Security is
defined by simulation. For every adversary corrupting at most \(t\) parties in
the real protocol, there is a simulator in an ideal world, where a trusted
party computes \(f\), such that the adversary's view together with the honest
parties' outputs is distributed identically (perfect security), statistically
close (statistical), or computationally indistinguishable (computational).
Two-party computation (2PC) is the case \(n=2\). Yao posed the two-party
problem (MPC-PAPER-1982-YAO); MPC-PAPER-1987-GMW and MPC-PAPER-1988-BGW gave
general protocols.

sections.heading: Core notions
sections.content:
- **Corruption threshold**: the bound \(t\) on corrupted parties. Honest
  majority means \(t<n/2\); dishonest majority allows up to \(t=n-1\).
- **Semi-honest versus malicious**: a semi-honest (passive) adversary follows
  the protocol but reads the corrupted parties' state; a malicious (active)
  adversary deviates arbitrarily.
- **Static, adaptive, proactive**: corruptions are fixed in advance, chosen
  during the run (MPC-PAPER-1996-ADAPTIVE), or move between epochs while shares
  are refreshed (MPC-PAPER-1995-PROACTIVE).
- **Output guarantees**: with security with abort, the adversary may learn the
  output and deny it to honest parties; identifiable abort also names a
  cheater; fairness gives everyone the output or no one; guaranteed output
  delivery (GOD) always gives honest parties the output. Fairness is
  impossible for general functions without an honest majority, although some
  functions admit it (MPC-PAPER-2010-FAIR).
- **Feasibility**: with private channels, perfect security holds for
  \(t<n/3\) malicious or \(t<n/2\) semi-honest corruptions
  (MPC-PAPER-1988-BGW); under computational assumptions, any \(t<n\) is
  possible with abort (MPC-PAPER-1987-GMW).
- **Network and composition**: synchronous or asynchronous networks
  (MPC-PAPER-1993-ASYNC); stand-alone or universally composable (UC) security
  (MPC-PAPER-2001-UC).
- **Preprocessing model**: an input-independent offline phase produces
  correlated randomness, such as multiplication triples or oblivious-transfer
  (OT) correlations, which a fast online phase consumes (MPC-PAPER-1991-BEAVER).
- **Representation**: Boolean or arithmetic circuits, with values held as
  garbled labels or as additive, Shamir, or replicated secret shares.

sections.heading: Main approaches
sections.content:
- **Garbled circuits**: one party encrypts the circuit gate by gate and another
  evaluates it, in a constant number of rounds (MPC-PAPER-1982-YAO;
  multiparty: MPC-PAPER-1990-BMR). Per-gate cost fell with free XOR
  (MPC-PAPER-2008-FREEXOR), half gates (MPC-PAPER-2015-HALFGATES), and about
  1.5 labels per AND gate (MPC-PAPER-2021-THREE-HALVES).
- **Secret-sharing evaluation**: linear gates are local and each multiplication
  costs interaction. GMW-style Boolean sharing uses OT for each AND gate;
  Shamir sharing gives information-theoretic honest-majority protocols,
  generalized to multiplicative linear secret-sharing schemes
  (MPC-PAPER-2000-CDM).
- **Authenticated preprocessing for dishonest majority**: information-theoretic
  MACs on shares, with triples produced by somewhat homomorphic encryption
  (MPC-PAPER-2011-SPDZ) or by OT (MPC-PAPER-2012-TINYOT,
  MPC-PAPER-2016-MASCOT).
- **Correlation generation**: OT extension from a few base OTs
  (MPC-PAPER-2003-IKNP) and pseudorandom correlation generators that expand
  short seeds locally (MPC-PAPER-2019-PCG, MPC-PAPER-2024-FOLEAGE,
  MPC-PAPER-2026-IKR-PCF).
- **Mixed protocols and frameworks**: conversions between arithmetic, Boolean,
  and garbled representations (MPC-PAPER-2015-ABY, MPC-PAPER-2018-ABY3,
  MPC-PAPER-2020-MOTION) and general frameworks (MPC-PAPER-2020-MPSPDZ).
  A 2019 survey compares eleven compilers by usability rather than speed
  and finds no standard benchmarks with which to measure them
  (MPC-PAPER-2019-SOK-COMPILERS).

sections.heading: Notation
sections.content:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(n\) | Number of parties |
| \(t\) | Maximum number of corrupted parties tolerated |

sections.heading: Scope of this atlas
sections.content:
This topic covers general-purpose 2PC and \(n\)-party MPC over Boolean,
arithmetic, or mixed circuits, against passive or active adversaries with
honest or dishonest majority. Threshold signatures, private set intersection,
and private machine learning appear only when they change a general
mechanism; MPC-in-the-head belongs to proof systems.
